description: S3 bucket policies must not grant access to untrusted principals

requirements.description: Bucket has no attached resource policy at all
requirements.rationale: With no policy present there are no allow statements, so no untrusted principal can be granted access via a bucket policy. The rule has nothing to evaluate.

requirements.description: Bucket policy contains only deny statements
requirements.rationale: Deny statements cannot grant access to any principal, trusted or otherwise. The rule targets allow grants to untrusted principals.

requirements.description: Bucket policy allow statement uses a wildcard principal with no conditions constraining who may assume that wildcard
requirements.rationale: A wildcard principal in an Allow statement grants access to anyone (including anonymous callers), which is the canonical untrusted-principal scenario per AWS S3 security guidance.

requirements.description: Bucket policy allow statement uses a wildcard principal but a condition narrows the effective identity to a trusted set (e.g., an organization ID, an explicit principal ARN allow-list, a specific VPC endpoint, or a specific source IP range)
requirements.rationale: Per the resolved decision, a restrictive condition that constrains the effective principal set to identifiable/trusted callers makes the grant auditable and specific, not open to untrusted parties. The condition must narrow identity; see REQ-18 for a condition that merely constrains the request.

requirements.description: Bucket policy allow statement uses a wildcard principal with a condition present, but that condition constrains a property of the request rather than which identities may use the grant (e.g., requiring encrypted transport or a particular canned ACL)
requirements.rationale: This is the complement of REQ-04, which passes only because the condition narrows the effective principal set. A condition on a request property leaves the grant reachable by every caller in the world, so treating the mere presence of a condition as sufficient would pass a world-readable bucket. Recording the near-miss explicitly keeps an implementation from satisfying REQ-04 by checking only that some condition exists.

requirements.description: Bucket policy allow statement grants access to a specific IAM principal identified by an ARN in a named AWS account (same-account or cross-account)
requirements.rationale: Per the resolved decision, a principal identified by an explicit ARN (and thus an explicit account) is a deliberate, auditable grant. The rule targets non-identifiable principals, not named ones.

requirements.description: Bucket policy allow statement grants access to an entire AWS account (account ID or root ARN) rather than an individual principal
requirements.rationale: An account-scoped grant names a specific, identifiable account. Per the resolved decision there is no trust list; explicit account identifiers are treated as intentional, auditable grants.

requirements.description: Bucket policy allow statement grants access to an AWS service principal with no condition restricting the source account or source ARN
requirements.rationale: Per the resolved decision, unrestricted service-principal grants can be invoked on behalf of any account's resources and constitute an untrusted grant unless narrowed by aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn.

requirements.description: Bucket policy allow statement grants access to an AWS service principal and a condition restricts the source account or the source ARN to a specific value
requirements.rationale: A source-account or source-ARN condition binds the service invocation to a specific caller resource, satisfying the confused-deputy mitigation and making the grant trusted.

requirements.description: Bucket policy allow statement grants access to a federated identity provider (SAML/OIDC) identified by a specific provider ARN
requirements.rationale: A federated principal identified by a specific provider ARN is an explicit, named trust relationship, analogous to naming an IAM principal.

requirements.description: Bucket policy allow statement omits any principal element
requirements.rationale: Per the resolved decision, an allow statement without a principal is not a valid IAM grant and would be rejected at deploy time, so it does not grant access to any principal.

requirements.description: Bucket policy contains multiple allow statements where at least one uses an unconstrained wildcard principal and others name specific principals
requirements.rationale: A single overly broad statement grants access to untrusted principals regardless of other well-scoped statements; the presence of specific grants elsewhere does not neutralize the wildcard grant.

requirements.description: Bucket policy allow statement principal value is a wildcard and the statement's Effect is unresolvable at analysis time
requirements.rationale: When the effect cannot be determined, the rule cannot assert that a wildcard-principal grant is actually an Allow. Passing avoids false positives on values not resolvable at analysis time.

requirements.description: Bucket policy allow statement grants access to a principal ARN whose account attribution cannot be resolved (e.g., dynamic or parameterized ARN without a determinable account segment)
requirements.rationale: Per the resolved decision, principals whose identity cannot be resolved at analysis time are not flagged, to avoid false positives on unresolvable values.

requirements.description: Bucket policy statements collection is present but empty
requirements.rationale: An empty statement list grants no access, so no untrusted-principal grant exists.

requirements.description: Bucket policy allow statement principal is expressed as a list that includes both a wildcard entry and specific principal identifiers, with no condition narrowing the wildcard
requirements.rationale: The wildcard entry within the principal list expands the grant to anyone regardless of the co-listed specific principals; the effective grant still reaches untrusted callers.

requirements.description: Bucket policy allow statement uses a wildcard principal combined with a Deny-style NotPrincipal exclusion of a specific identity
requirements.rationale: Excluding one identity from a wildcard Allow still leaves the grant open to essentially every other principal in the world, which is not a trusted-principal grant.

requirements.description: Bucket policy allow statement grants access to a canonical user identifier (e.g., an S3 CanonicalUser value) explicitly listed
requirements.rationale: A canonical user ID names a specific AWS account holder, so the grant is auditable and directed at a named principal rather than an untrusted wildcard.
